convoLines.text: "We're eating through stores faster than we replace them. Will you forage with me tomorrow? Two pairs of eyes, twice the ground."
"The stores won't stretch past tomorrow, and I'm not choosing who eats. Meet me at the south slope below the meadow and we'll fill packs before dark."
There is no playable joint foraging outing yet. Giving food does not perform the promised outing.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Juan owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them Groundnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"They're already drifting away. "Later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"What are you hoping for? Not the big stuff. The small thing. You know?"
"Tell you what — God, yes. That's the dream now. Eight hours of not being afraid."
"Listen — Still on what you're hoping for."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"...I should say, I trade in what I know. My knowledge for yours. Or food, if you're short on secrets."
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Since Juan died... I keep expecting to see Juan at the fire. Stupid."
"I keep turning over the last thing Juan said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
You show them Groundnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"About the pantry run — I still haven't found anyone. Any chance?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Juan always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"The fire feels smaller without Juan. The rest of us will have to be bigger."
"I tend the fire without being asked for Juan, now. Feels right. Feels like the least I can do."
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them White Oak Acorns — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"Good — what's been happening, settled. Feels better said out loud."
"...Actually, forget it."
"About that question — Has this changed you? Like, fundamentally? You doing okay?"
"The old you got you here. The new you keeps you here. Both count. How are you holding up, though?"
"Still on how this changed you."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Last time things were different. They always are." "Juan is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"My part? I remember them. Someone has to do it properly."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
You show them Jerusalem Artichoke — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
A warmth settles over the conversation — they lean in a little.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"...Actually, forget it."
"Can we talk?" Sanjay sits down near you. "Just... talk. Like people used to."
They light up a little when they see you.
"What's something from your old life that's actually useful here?"
"Can I be honest? Not dumb at all. The people who can't wait are the ones who make mistakes. You're an asset."
"If I may — Still on your useful old-life skills."
"Can I trust you? I mean really."
"That's the right answer. The wrong one would've been 'yes' too fast. That is all."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? Anyway — how are YOU doing?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "The Tide Clock. They just... took Nora. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"Anyway." A small smile.
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"Hah. What do you miss most? From before."
"God. Yes. I dream about soup. Actual soup, with a spoon."
"Still on what you miss most. I'm sure it'll be fine."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"They took Nora — The Tide Clock, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
You show them Groundnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Same weather, different day. I keep notes."
"Same as always: we endure."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
